content:
The [Mean Median Mode Calculator](/mean-median-mode-calculator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Find mean, median, mode, range and quartiles for any list of numerical observations. Enter your numbers (separate with commas, spaces or new lines) and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Mean, median and mode describe the centre of a data set in different ways. The mean uses every value, the median identifies the middle after sorting, and the mode identifies the most frequent observations. Showing them together helps reveal skew and outliers that a single average can hide. This tool also reports range, quartiles, count and sum so the distribution can be checked without a spreadsheet. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers.

## How to use the Mean Median Mode Calculator

Start by typing or pasting your numbers (separate with commas, spaces or new lines). The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. The steps below walk through each input in order.

1. Paste observations separated by commas, spaces, semicolons or line breaks.
2. Check the reported count to ensure every intended value was recognised.
3. Compare mean with median, inspect any modes, and use quartiles and range to understand spread.

## Formula

Mean = Σx ÷ n. Median is the central sorted value or the average of the two central values. Mode = value(s) with greatest frequency. Range = maximum − minimum.

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [Mean Median Mode Calculator](/mean-median-mode-calculator) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. For 12, 15, 15, 18, 22, 25, 29 and 31, the mean is 20.875, the median is 20, the mode is 15 and the range is 19. Try the same figures in the [Mean Median Mode Calculator](/mean-median-mode-calculator) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves.

With the default values (Numbers (separate with commas, spaces or new lines): 12, 15, 15, 18, 22, 25, 29, 31), the [Mean Median Mode Calculator](/mean-median-mode-calculator) returns Mean: 20.875, Median: 20, Mode: 15, Range: 19, First quartile (Q1): 15, Third quartile (Q3): 27, Count and sum: 8 values; sum 167. ## Why the mean and median differ

A very large observation pulls the mean upward but moves the median little or not at all. For household income, house prices and other skewed data, the median often better represents a typical observation. For roughly symmetric measurements without extreme outliers, the mean makes efficient use of every value.

## Quartiles and multimodal data

Q1 is the median of the lower half and Q3 the median of the upper half, excluding the overall median from an odd-sized data set. Several values can tie as modes; the tool lists all of them. If no observation repeats, it reports no repeated mode rather than calling every value a mode.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Always sort before finding a median by hand.
- Use median alongside mean when extreme values are present.
- Quartile conventions differ slightly between software packages, especially for small samples.

## Frequently asked questions

### Can a data set have more than one mode?

Yes. If several different values share the highest frequency, all are modes. The calculator lists every tied value. You can use it as often as you like, and because nothing is uploaded, stored or tracked, there is nothing to delete afterwards.

### What if every number occurs once?

There is no repeated mode. Although some descriptions call every value modal, reporting no repeated mode is usually clearer for analysis. Try it with your own numbers in the [Mean Median Mode Calculator](/mean-median-mode-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Which average should I use?

Use mean for additive numerical analysis, median for a robust typical value with outliers, and mode for the most common value or category. Try it with your own numbers in the [Mean Median Mode Calculator](/mean-median-mode-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.
